text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Food and detergent company Unilever's shares soar six percent on higher than expected Q3 profits. (p1)
- Food and beverages group BolsWessanen and food company
CSM deny rumours of impending merger. (p1)
- Danish Shipowner Maersk wants its own container terminal on Rotterdam's Maasvlakte by 1999. (p1)
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm puts forward bill proposing tighter rules against insider trading. (p1)
- October consumer prices rise 0.3 pct month-on-month and 2.4 pct year-on-year. (p1)
- Hungarian privatisation bureau agrees to sell 89.23 pct stake in Magyar Hitel Bank to ABN Amro bank. (p1)
- Philips Electronics settles lawsuit brought by video rental chain Super Club founder Maurits de Prins. (p3)
- Shipbuilder IHC Caland has received up to Dfl 545 million worth of orders since the middle of the year. (p4)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Coalition parties in favour of setting aside money in order to finance OAPs' benefits in the future. (p1)
- Senior editor of newspaper Haagsche Courant threatened with death by extreme right party NVU. (p1)
- Investment company HAL makes a bid of Dfl 80 million on certificates of newspaper Het Financieele Dagblad. (p2)
- Hollandia Kloos' director Rob Lubbers sees potential in harbour concern Furness he bought from Pakhoed. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Dutch national soccer team squashes Wales 7-1. (p1)
- Anti-alcohol ad featuring champagne stopped after French ambassador's complaints. (p1)
- 110 vehicles at Heineken brewery in Zaire looted. (p3)
- Steel concern Hoogovens thinks the introduction of Europe's single currency Euro will be an opportunity to reduce fluctuations in results. (p13)
TROUW
- Cities appeal to cabinet to confirm route marked out for High-Speed rail link through the "Green Heart". (p4)
- Dutch government should use its EU presidency starting Jan. 1 to put urgent trade issues with the U.S. on the agenda, says chemicals giant DSM's chief S. de Bree. (p4)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- South Korea's government directs own inquiry into Samsung's takeover plans of Fokker. (p11)
